academic_translation:
Whatever is seen, heard, and known
Is not what is to be negated here;
Here, the conceptualization of true existence,
Which is the cause of suffering, is to be overturned.
translation: I am not denying the things you see, hear, and know. I only want to stop you from thinking things are truly real. That is the cause of suffering.

academic_translation:
If an illusion is not other than the mind,
And it is not conceived as non-other either,
If it is an entity, how is it not other?
If it is not other, it does not exist as an entity.
translation: Someone might say an illusion is not different from the mind. But they also say it is not exactly the same. If it is a real thing, how is it not different? If it is not different, it does not exist as a thing.

academic_translation:
Just as an illusion, although not true,
Is something to be seen, so too the mind is the one who sees.
"If saṃsāra is based on an entity,
Otherwise it would be like space."
translation: Someone might say an illusion is not true, but we still see it. They say the mind is the one who sees. They might argue the cycle of rebirth must be based on a real thing. Otherwise, it would just be like empty space.

academic_translation:
Since a non-entity depends on an entity,
How could it be endowed with a function?
Your mind, without a companion,
Would become entirely solitary.
translation: But if a non-existent thing depends on a real thing, how could it do anything? Without anything outside it, your mind would have no companion. Your mind would become completely alone.

academic_translation:
When the mind is free of an apprehended object,
At that time, all are Tathāgatas.
Even if that is so, what benefit is there
In conceptually constructing Cittamātra?
translation: When the mind is free of any thing the mind takes in, everyone becomes a Thus-Gone One. Even if this were true, what is the good of it? What is the point of making up the idea of Mind Only?

academic_translation:
"Even if one knows things to be like an illusion,
How will the afflictions be averted?
Since, toward an illusory woman,
Even her creator generates attachment."
translation: Someone might ask: Even if you know things are like an illusion, how will that stop troubling emotions? Think of a magician who creates a woman made by illusion. Even the magician can still feel clinging toward her.

academic_translation:
Her creator, toward objects of knowledge,
Has not abandoned the latent tendencies of the afflictions.
Therefore, when he sees her,
His latent tendency of emptiness is weak.
translation: That magician has not let go of his deep habits of troubling emotions toward things to know. Because of this, when he sees her, his deep habit of emptiness is very weak.

academic_translation:
Through habituation to the latent tendency of emptiness,
The latent tendency of entities will be abandoned;
And through habituation to "there is nothing at all,"
That too will later be abandoned.

locked_terms.use: habit left in the mind by things

translation: If you keep getting used to the habit of emptiness, you will let go of the habit left in the mind by things. By getting used to thinking "there is nothing," you will later let go of that deep habit too.

academic_translation:
When one asserts, "Such and such does not exist,"
And the entity to be analyzed is not apprehended,
At that time, how can a non-entity lacking a basis
Remain before the intellect?
translation: When you say, "This thing does not exist," and you cannot find the thing you are looking for, what happens? How can a non-existent thing without a base stay in front of the thinking mind?

academic_translation:
When entities and non-entities
Do not remain before the intellect,
At that time, since there is no other aspect,
There is thorough pacification in non-apprehension.
translation: When a thing and a non-existent thing do not stay in front of the thinking mind, there is no other way it appears. At that time, by having no object of focus, there is complete calm.

academic_translation:
Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-fulfilling tree
Completely fulfill hopes,
Likewise, to the ones to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers,
The form of the Victor appears.
translation: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree completely grant our hopes. In the same way, the form of the Victorious One appears to the one to be guided through the power of a wishing prayer.

academic_translation:
For example, just as when a garuḍa shrine
Has been accomplished and its creator has passed away,
Even though a long time has elapsed since he passed,
It pacifies poison and so forth.
translation: For example, a shrine for the great sky bird might be built. Even a long time after the builder passes away, it still clears away poison and other harms.

academic_translation:
Likewise, in accordance with the conduct of awakening,
The shrine of the Victor, too, has been accomplished;
Even when the bodhisattva has passed
Into nirvāṇa, it accomplishes all aims.
translation: In the same way, following the way of acting for awakening, the shrine of the Victorious One has been built. Even after the awakening hero passes away, it still achieves every goal.

academic_translation:
"If offerings are made to one without a mind,
How will they be endowed with a result?"
Because whether he remains or has passed into nirvāṇa,
It is taught that it is exactly the same.
translation: Someone might ask, "If we make offerings to someone without a mind, how will we get a result?" It is because the teachings say it is exactly the same whether the Buddha stays here or has passed into freedom from sorrow.

academic_translation:
Whether in conventional truth or in reality,
It is acceptable, for that result is from scripture,
Just as, for example, toward a true Buddha,
It is endowed with a result.
translation: Whether in everyday truth or in the way things really are, this makes sense. The sacred text says a result comes from it. It brings a result just like giving to a real Buddha.

academic_translation:
"Liberation comes from seeing the truths;
What is the use of seeing emptiness?"
Because scripture states that without this path,
There is no awakening.
translation: Someone might say, "Freedom comes from seeing the truths. Why do we need to see emptiness?" The sacred text says that without this path, there is no awakening.

academic_translation:
"If the Mahāyāna is not established,
How is your scripture established?"
"Because this is established for both of us."
Initially, this was not established for you.
translation: Someone might ask, "If the Great Vehicle is not proven, how is your sacred text proven?" You might answer, "Because we both agree on it." But at first, it was not proven for you either.

academic_translation:
By whatever conditions you believe in that,
That is the same for the Mahāyāna as well.
If it is true because any two other parties accept it,
The Vedas and so forth would also be true.
translation: Whatever circumstance makes you believe in your text is the same for the Great Vehicle. If a text is true just because two groups accept it, then the Vedas and other books would also be true.

academic_translation:
"If you say it is because the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute,"
Regarding scripture, there is dispute with non-Buddhists,
And regarding other scriptures, with your own and other schools;
Since they are subject to dispute, they would be discarded.
translation: Someone might say, "We reject the Great Vehicle because people argue about it." But you argue with a non-Buddhist about your sacred text. You also argue with other groups about other sacred texts. Since people argue about them, you would have to throw them all away.

academic_translation:
If being a monk is the root of the teaching,
Even being a monk is difficult to establish.
For those whose minds have apprehension,
Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
translation: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, even being a monk is hard to prove. For people whose minds are holding on to things, even freedom from sorrow is hard to reach.

academic_translation:
If one is liberated by abandoning afflictions,
It would occur immediately after that.
Even without afflictions, in them
The power of karma is seen.
translation: If someone is set free just by giving up troubling emotion, they would be free right away. But even without troubling emotion, we still see the power of action in them.

academic_translation:
If you say it is certain that, for the time being,
The craving that is the cause of grasping does not exist,
Even if that craving is not afflicted,
Why would it not exist, just like delusion?
translation: Someone might say it is certain that, for now, the wanting that causes holding on does not exist. Even if that wanting is not troubled by troubling emotion, why would it not exist? It would be just like confusion.

academic_translation:
Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling,
And feeling also exists in them.
A mind that has apprehension
Will remain fixed upon something.
translation: Wanting happens due to the circumstance of feeling. And those people still have feeling. A mind that is fixing on something will remain stuck on something.

academic_translation:
A mind that is devoid of emptiness,
Though ceased, will arise again,
Like the meditative absorption of non-perception;
Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
translation: A mind that does not have emptiness will start up again even after it stops. It is like a deep meditation with no perceiving. Because of this, you should meditate on emptiness.

academic_translation:
If any speech that enters the sūtras
Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha,
Is it not asserted that most of the Mahāyāna
Is equal to your sūtras?
translation: If you say that any speech found in a scripture was spoken by the Buddha, do you not agree that most of the Great Vehicle is equal to your teaching texts?

academic_translation:
If, due to a single unincluded one,
All become faulty,
Then due to a single one similar to a sūtra,
Why are they not all spoken by the Victor?
translation: You say that leaving out one text makes them all faulty. But what if one is like a true teaching text? Why are they not all spoken by the Victorious One?

academic_translation:
Any speech whose depth was unfathomed
By Mahākāśyapa and the rest,
Because you do not understand it,
Who would make it unacceptable?
translation: Even Mahakashyapa and others could not measure the depth of these words. Just because you do not understand them, who would make them unacceptable?

academic_translation:
For the sake of those suffering through delusion,
Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear,
Remaining in saṃsāra is accomplished—
This is the result of emptiness.
translation: We want to help those who have suffering from confusion. So, we are freed from extreme clinging and fear. We can now stay in the cycle of rebirth. This is the result of emptiness.

academic_translation:
Thus, toward the position of emptiness,
Refutation is not tenable.
Therefore, without any doubt,
One should meditate on emptiness.
translation: You cannot succeed in proving wrong the position of emptiness. Therefore, without any doubt, you should meditate on emptiness.

academic_translation:
Of the obscuration of afflictions and of objects of knowledge,
Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness.
By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient,
How could it not be meditated upon?

locked_terms.use: veil of troubling emotions and of things to know

translation: There is a dark veil of troubling emotions and of things to know. Emptiness is the remedy for this darkness. If you wish to quickly become all-knowing, how could you not meditate on it?

academic_translation:
Whatever thing produces suffering,
If fear arises from that,
Emptiness pacifies suffering;
How could fear arise toward it?
translation: If a thing produces suffering, fear will arise from it. But emptiness calms suffering. How could fear arise toward it?

academic_translation:
If any self existed,
one might become afraid of anything;
but since no self exists at all,
who is there to be afraid?
translation: If any self existed, a person might be afraid of anything. But since no self exists at all, who is there to be afraid?

academic_translation:
Teeth, hair, and nails are not the self,
and the self is not bones or blood;
it is not mucus, nor is it phlegm,
and it is neither lymph nor pus.
translation: Teeth, hair, and nails are not the self, and the self is not bones or blood. It is not mucus or phlegm, and it is not lymph or pus.

academic_translation:
The self is not fat or sweat,
and the lungs and liver are not the self;
other internal organs are also not the self,
and the self is not feces or urine.
translation: The self is not fat or sweat, and the lungs and liver are not the self. Other inside organs are also not the self, and the self is not feces or urine.

academic_translation:
Flesh and skin are not the self,
and warmth and wind are not the self;
the orifices are not the self, and in all ways,
the six consciousnesses are not the self either.
translation: Flesh and skin are not the self, and warmth and wind are not the self. The openings of the body are not the self. In all ways, the six kinds of awareness are not the self either.
If the awareness of sound were lasting forever, it would hear sound all the time. If there is no thing to know, what does it know? Why would it be called an awareness?

academic_translation:
If that which does not cognize were consciousness,
it would follow that a piece of wood is consciousness too;
therefore, it is certain that without the presence
of an object of knowledge, there is no consciousness.
translation: If something that does not know anything were an awareness, then a piece of wood would be an awareness too. Therefore, it is certain that without a thing to know, there is no awareness.

academic_translation:
If that very thing knows form,
Why does it not also hear at that time?
If it is because sound is not nearby,
Then the consciousness of that is also absent.
translation: If that exact same thing knows a shape, why does it not hear at the same time? Someone might say it is because a sound is not close by. But if that is true, then its awareness of the sound is gone too.

academic_translation:
Whatever has the nature of apprehending sound,
How could it become the apprehender of form?
One person is designated as a father and a son,
But this is not true reality.
translation: If something is made to notice a sound, how could it become the thing that notices a shape? One person can be labelled as both a father and a son. But that is not what is truly real.

academic_translation:
Thus, sattva, rajas, and
Tamas are neither a son nor a father,
And that apprehender of form is not seen to have a nature
That possesses the apprehension of sound.
translation: So, brightness, restlessness, and darkness are neither a son nor a father. And the thing that notices a shape is not seen to have a nature that notices a sound.
